chunks.text:
In this technical specification, Potential supplier/the Contractor means an individual engaged in entrepreneurial  activities,  a  legal  entity  (with  the  exception  of  state  institutions,  unless  otherwise provided for them by the laws of the Republic of Kazakhstan), a temporary association of  legal entities (consortium) that claims to conclude a Contract on procurement of complex works on surveys, design, logistical  support  and  «turnkey»  construction  (hereinafter  referred  to  as  the  Contract)  with  «CCGT Turkistan» LLP (hereinafter referred to as the Customer).
The  Contractor  undertakes  to  carry  out  complex  work  on  design,  logistical  support  and construction on a «turnkey» basis under the project «Construction of  a power plant on the basis of  CCGT (combined cycle gas turbine) with a capacity of 1000 MW in the Turkestan region. Main site», which must be performed in accordance with the terms of the Contract, this document and other conditions with access to full design capacity (hereinafter referred to as the Works referred to in the Contract as the «Facility / Works»).
All terms in this document should be interpreted in accordance with the definitions of  such terms provided for  in the Contract  (in the Contract Agreement and General Conditions), unless otherwise specified in this technical specification and its appendices.
The work shall consist of the design, procurement, construction, inspection, testing, the process of pre-commissioning works  (PCW) to bring it up to  production capacity with the development of a project for PCW, commissioning, all and any actions necessary to deliver to the Customer a complete, safe, functional, operable and maintained power plant.
Any design, material, method or equipment provided by the Contractor shall be fit for purpose and meet all requirements of  the Contract.
No  deficiencies,  errors  or  omissions  in  this  document  with  respect  to  any  design,  material, method, equipment or specification contained therein shall release the Contractor from his obligation to perform the Work under the Contract.
The  Contractor  shall  be  deemed  to  have  included in  the  Contract  Price  all  installations  and equipment, whether or not specifically specified herein, that are necessary to form a complete Facility, fit in all respects for its intended use.
Works include,  but are not limited to,  design,  obtaining  permits  and  approvals,  obtaining  all required expertise certificates, manufacturing, construction, supply,  in-process  testing,  packaging for export, shipping and unloading, transportation, delivery to the Facility, unloading at the Facility, storage on and off the Facility, full construction, connection to existing infrastructure (network) or construction of new  infrastructure,  conservation,  putting  into  operation  and  commissioning,  performance  and reliability tests upon completion of  works, including tools and equipment for maintenance and operation, spare parts, instruction / training of  the Customer's personnel and liabilities for the defect liability period for equipment required for a fully functioning Facility.
label: text

chunks.text:
The Contractor shall provide all equipment, scope of  work and services, as specified, in order to make  the  Facility  fully  completed  and  functional  for  safe,  reliable,  serviceable  and  suitable  for commercial operation under all conditions and relations.
The Contractor shall provide full details of the labor resources he offers during construction periods to be included in the defined scope of work.
All materials and equipment must be new and of  the best quality for use under the conditions and fluctuations  in  temperature  and  pressure  that  will  be  encountered  in  operation,  without  excessive corrosion,  change in shape,  aging or fatigue,  and without undue stress or deformation in any part that may affect efficiency and reliability of a plant that is in all respects suitable for its intended purpose. No repairs will be permitted without the written permission of the Customer. Complete information on the properties and the thermal, chemical and mechanical treatments used must be provided.
Particular care must be taken to eliminate the  possibility of corrosion due to galvanic effects. Design, material selection and all installation methods should be such as to minimize these effects.
All parts of the installation that come into contact with potable water, industrial water or waste water,  such as pumps, pipes, heat exchangers, measuring instruments, etc., must be designed in such a way as to prevent contamination and corrosion. The same applies to individual plant equipment exposed to humid gases below the dew point.
q/
All  materials  to  be  used  in  the  Project  must  be  accompanied  by  the  necessary  certificates confirming their required quality in accordance with relevant international and local standards. These certificates must be presented to the Customer for verification.
All materials,  installations  and  equipment  must  be  suitable  for  the  purposes  of the  Facility. Equipment must be selected to ensure high reliability and availability of the entire Facility  with low levels of downtime and minimal maintenance. There must be permanent, safe access to all parts of the installation for inspections, operation and maintenance.
The construction of a power plant on the basis of CCGT with a capacity of 1000 MW in the Turkestan region includes all of the following works that are described or implied in this Technical Specification, as well as all matters not taken into account in it, which may be considered necessary for completion of works, further stable, safe, reliable and efficient exploitation, whether or not specified in this document.

The main equipment of  the Facility includes: a gas turbine (GT) with an electric generator, a heat recovery steam generators (HRSG), a steam turbine (ST) with an electric generator, a bypass and a chimney.
The main fuel is fuel gas, emergency (back-up) fuel is diesel fuel.

chunks.text:
The power of a maneuverable Power plant is determined by the requirements for installed and control power, the characteristics of  industrially developed gas turbine equipment.
The defining factors are:  high maneuverability with a large control range and maintaining the efficiency of the equipment in the control range while reducing power to a technical minimum.
For the Facility, due to the significant influence of  the outside air temperature on the GT power, the nominal and maximum power values and the limits of the control range change significantly with the change in the outside air temperature.
The indicators of installed capacity and maneuverability for each type of power equipment are determined in the Project by the technical characteristics of the equipment and are specified during the annual certification of power units.
The installed electrical power of condensing combined cycle plants is determined as the sum of the  capacities  of steam  and  gas  turbines  at  an  average  annual  temperature,  air  humidity  and  the corresponding temperature of the cooling water.
The determination of the average annual generation of electrical energy was made on the basis of  simulated graphs of  the dependence of  electrical power on the ambient temperature (Figure 1.3.1). In doing so, it is accepted:
Figure 1.3.1.
- «base» mode of operation is taken below the technical minimum;
- within the regulation range, the coefficient of influence of the participation of equipment in the regulation of  daily schedules of  electrical loads (0.5) was applied to the volume of  electricity generation.

The main fuel that provides production activities for the generation of  electricity of  the designed Facility, is fuel (natural and associated) gas provided by «QazaqGaz» JSC from two sources:
- Main gas pipeline (MGP) «Beineu-Bozoi-Shymkent» (main);
- -Main gas pipeline (MGP) «BGR-TBA» (reserve).
To provide the projected power plant with fuel gas, the construction of the linear part of  the gas pipeline-outlet with AGDS was considered, which ensures the transportation and supply of natural gas with the declared volume of consumption.
The equipment of  the external gas supply system includes the following units:
- security crane units (SCU);
- cleaning device launch unit (CDLU), cleaning device receiving unit (CDRU);
- automated gas distribution station (AGDS);
- gas pipeline.
Power supply of  the site AGDS - «CCGT», CDRU, CDLU, SCU is carried out from the projected OTLPW-10 kV (overhead transmission lines with protected wires) for auxiliary needs of the CCGT.
Steel  pipes  of the  gas  pipeline  provide  for  measures  to  protect  engineering  networks  from corrosion.  The  external  gas supply  complex  is provided with  communication  and signaling  systems: fiber optic communication, industrial and technological USW  (ultra-short waves) radio communication, satellite communication, IP telephony, burglar alarm, fire alarm, video surveillance.
The complex of  all measures to ensure the reliable operation of  all units of  the gas supply system makes it possible to ensure uninterrupted supply of  fuel gas from the main gas pipeline to the site of  the designed combined-cycle plant with the required parameters.
fOCT 305-82 (GOST 305-82) diesel fuel is provided as an emergency fuel for gas turbines.
For the storage of a 3 -day supply of fuel, a diesel fuel warehouse is provided, the total capacity is determined by the project. A diesel fuel pumping station is provided for receiving and pumping diesel fuel.
To replenish the emergency reserve of  diesel fuel, it is transported by road and/or rail to the sites.

Estimated fire extinguishing consumption is the total consumption for external and internal fire extinguishing for the main building 162 1/s, including 100 1/s for external fire extinguishing, 62 1/s for internal fire extinguishing with a design head of70.0 wcm (water column meters).
The  water  consumption  for  external  fire  extinguishing  of the  projected  main  building  is determined depending on the volume of1030.7 thousand m 3 , the degree of  fire resistance - II, fire hazard category  B  1  in  accordance  with  Table  1  of Appendix  5  to  the  Technical  regulation  «General requirements for fire safety», for internal fire extinguishing - according to table 2 of  CIT PK 4.01-1012012  «BHyTJ)eHHHH  ao.n;orrpoao.n;  H  KamUima�m1  3,D;amrii  H  coopy)KeHHii»  (SP  RK  4.01-101-2012 «Internal water supply and sewerage of  buildings and structures»).
To  provide  external  and  internal  fire  extinguishing  at  the  site  of the  power  plant,  a  fire extinguishing pumping station and fire-fighting water tanks are provided.
The pumping station provides for the installation of  two groups of  pumps:
- two fire pumps (working, standby) with a capacity of  580-600 m 3 /h, head 80 wcm;
- two pumps for supplying water to the drinking water treatment plant and boiler feeding water treatment plant, with a capacity of  650.0 m 3 /h, a head of  40.0 wcm.
The capacity of  the tanks is taken from the condition of  the duration of  the fire extinguishing of the main building for 3 hours, the water supply for the boiler  make-up water treatment plant and the drinking water treatment plant.
The estimated volume of  tanks is 2400 m 3 , 2 tanks of  1200 m 3 are accepted.
The maximum period for the restoration of the fire volume of water, in  accordance with the requirement ofCHHil PK 4.01-02-2001 (SNiP RK 4.01-02-2001), should be no more than 36 hours. The estimated water consumption during the restoration of  the fire-fighting volume will be 48.5 m 3 /hour.

Effluent from sanitary appliances of  the designed buildings is diverted to the domestic sewerage network. The volume of  domestic wastewater disposal is equal to the volume of  water consumption and is 75.0 m 3 /hour, 300.0 m 3 /day.
Household wastewater flows by gravity into a sewage pumping station with a capacity of  75.0 m 3 /hour,  factory-made,  with subsequent supply to treatment facilities.  A station for deep biological treatment of  domestic wastewater is provided at the site of  the power plant. Wastewater treatment plant of  prefabricated modular  design,  with  a capacity  of 300 m 3 per  day.  Treatment facilities operate in automatic  mode.  The  treatment  facilities  include a  block  of biological  treatment,  post-treatment of wastewater on the filter, disinfection and sludge treatment.
Water after treatment at the plant must meet the quality requirements for discharge into fishery water bodies.
Treated domestic wastewater after treatment facilities, depending on the quality of  treated water, can be used for irrigation of  green spaces and roads. Issues related to the use of  purified water should be resolved  with the  participation  of sanitary  protection  authorities.  If  the  water  quality  does  not meet sanitary requirements, the treated effluents are sent to the evaporation site.
Gravity networks of  household sewerage are provided from polyethylene pipes.

The total amount of  effluents entering the evaporation site is 1876.0 thousand m 3 /year.

The layout of the general plan of the power plant should be carried out so that the power plant fits on the allocated site for construction.

The main strategy for the construction of  a power plant based on a CCGT unit with a capacity of 1000 MW in the Turkestan region is to ensure the balance reliability of  the energy system of  the Republic of Kazakhstan, cover irregular fluctuations in the electrical load and power flow imbalances resulting from uneven power output from renewable  energy  sources,  increase  the reliability and safety of the power plant through the use of  modem technologies for the production of  electrical energy. All technical solutions must take into account the seismic hazard of  the region.
It is planned to build a new power plant based on modem types of CCGT, which will meet the requirements  of high  maneuverability  with  a  large control  range  and  maintaining  the  efficiency  of equipment operation in the control range while reducing power to a technical minimum. Implementation is provided on the territory of  the Turkestan region.
In order to optimize the construction time of the power plant, it is planned to carry out parallel work on the main CCGT site and external infrastructure facilities (power generation of  the electric power system, water intake system, access road, railway line and gas supply).
This Technical specification provides for works related to the construction of  the main site.

chunks.text:
The power plant will be used as a source of electrical energy. The basic mode of operation of  the power plant must ensure the issuance of electrical energy in accordance with the balance of electrical energy agreed by the Customer.
The Contractor must also indicate in his proposal the maximum possible output of electricity to the network in each of the modes of operation of the power plant. The characteristics of the auxiliary equipment  of the  power  units  should  allow  the  operation  of the  GT,  ST  based  on  the  maximum characteristics of  the GT, ST.
The operating mode required for the power plant is  at  least 350 starts/year. All requirements listed  in  ST  RK  ISO  14661-2011  apply  to  equipment  supplied  by  the  Contractor.  The  interval  of inspections and repairs of high-temperature parts of the gas path is at least 8000 hours. The resource before  the  first  overhaul  and  between  major  repairs  is  at  least  24000  hours.  The  interval  between maintenance is at least 1500 hours.
The power plant must ensure stable operation in the event of short circuits on the 220-500 kV overhead lines extending from the buses of  the CCGT Main site. The duration of  such work is set by the settings for the operation of relay  protection and automation (RP  A) without disconnecting the power plant from the network.
It is necessary to provide the ability to control reactive power (Q=const) at the point of  common connection. The reactive power control system must be designed in such a way that the reactive power setpoint is controlled at the point of common connection. The set point must be adjusted in steps of 1 MV  Ar within the technical limits, according to the P curve valid at the point of common connection. The error limit of  reactive power measurement at the point of common connection must be higher than +/-1 MVAr  .
.  The second reactive power control option (U=const) must provide voltage regulation at the point of  common connection. The control system must be arranged in such a way as to use the entire reactive power reserve  within  the technical  limits according to the P/Q  curve in order to  achieve  the voltage setting. The voltage  regulation dead zone is +/-1 kV at the point of common connection. The setting must be  adjusted in  steps  of 1 kV.  Voltage  regulation systems  must  be  designed in  such  a way that simultaneous  voltage  regulation does not  cause  instability in operation (voltage fluctuations,  control conflict).

The  sharply  continental  climate  of  the  Republic  of  Kazakhstan  and,  accordingly,  low temperatures  in  winter  and  high  temperatures  in  summer,  require  taking  into  account  the  range  of ambient temperatures at which the operation of the equipment is planned, temperature minimum/maximum ° C, atmospheric pressure at the height of  a particular site, on which the power of gas turbines depends.
With an increase in temperature in summer mode, the power of the GT is significantly reduced, so when switching from +  15C to +  30C, the power drop can be ~ 11-12% of the nominal one. In this case, the GT will not be able to produce the required power declared during certification.
An increase in the level of  the site and, as a result, a decrease in atmospheric pressure leads to a decrease in the power of  the GT.
An increase in temperature and an increase in altitude above sea level have a cumulative effect on the power of  the GT.

The value of the certified working electric power of the power plant (Prab) is determined by the technical characteristics  of the CCGT equipment during  the annual certification of the  power  of the power plant, taking into account  the  conditions of the  construction site (barometric pressure, current outdoor temperature).
In order to ensure  the specified  control  range,  the average hourly  power of a  CCGT  with a maneuverable generation mode is allowed no more than 0.5 of the control power.
The technical minimum also includes an environmental minimum that meets the requirements for NOx emissions at the lowest possible power.
The use of  the CCGT control range, taking into account the technical minimum, allows the use of  industrial gas turbines, instead of  aircraft derivatives, the use of  a standard maintenance schedule and repair periods without increasing the equivalent operating hours with frequent starts. The assessment of the  cost of  the entire life  cycle of  a maneuverable power plant includes both capital costs and service costs, taking into account the requirements for the number of  starts.
For the industrial gas turbines under consideration, the requirement of  at least 350 starts/year can only be achieved by significantly reducing the overhaul period and the service life of  the plants, which is inappropriate. The optimal solution for the tasks of the widest regulation is the aircraft-derived GT, operating in a simple cycle, if  necessary.
Industrial grade GT have different wear rates in base mode and in cyclic mode.
Thermal mechanical fatigue is the life limiting factor for peak duty units, while creep, oxidation and corrosion are life limiting factors for base duty units.
The maintenance interval is determined by which criterion limit is reached first.
The  normal  start-up  cycle  of a  CCGT  unit  from  a  cold  state  to  a  full  load  of 100%  1s approximately 4 hours.
The normal start-up cycle of  a CCGT unit from a hot state, in which less than 8 hours have passed from the moment of  shutdown to the moment of  start-up, until reaching 100% load, is approximately 2.5 hours. At the same time, a set of  approximately 80% of  the power takes about 30-40 minutes. With the use of modem methods, this time can be significantly reduced. The more powerful the equipment, the longer it will start.
Fast start in a simple cycle from any state applies only to aircraft-derived GT and some industrial GT up to 100 MW. It is these GT in a simple cycle that are most often used in world practice to solve the problems of  ensuring network flexibility and emergency backup of  renewable energy sources.

The HRSG is a drum boiler with natural circulation in high and low pressure evaporative circuits, single-shell, horizontal profile,  suspended from its own frame through intermediate metal structures, with a deaerator built into the LP drum. The framework is executed on high-strength bolts.
To ensure the operation of the GT in open cycle mode (when the HRSG is off), the HRSG is equipped with a bypass system including:
- bypass valve (divertor);
- shut-off  valve guillotine type;
- -a  bypass  chimney  with  stairs,  platforms,  built-in  silencer,  light  protection  and  lightning protection.
The HRSG is designed to operate on combustion products coming from the GT. The main and reserve fuel for GT is dry natural gas. Emergency fuel - diesel.
The main HRSG equipment is installed in the building.
For  access  and  ease  of maintenance  of equipment  and  fittings,  stairs  and  platforms  with galvanized flooring are provided.
The maximum gas temperature at the inlet to the HRSG is 580 °C (to be specified after receiving data on the GT).
The HRSG and flues are made gas-tight, based on the excess gas pressure of 3.5 kPa. The way to ensure gas tightness is sheathing and sealing.
The heating surfaces of the HRSG are made of  pipes with external slotted and continuous spiral­ band finning. The location of  the heat exchange pipes of  the heating surfaces is vertical.
The HRSG design provides complete drainage of heating surfaces and pipelines, as well as the possibility of  pre-start, operational, chemical and water flushing, conservation.
The HRSG layout provides for places for tracing cable routes, impulse pipes, and also provides the ability to install the necessary measuring devices, fittings, fittings, bosses and other selected devices for CMI, automation and protection in places convenient for maintenance.
The wall material of  the high-pressure drum is selected from the condition of  the minimum startup time of  the HRSG from a cold state.
The HRSG has manual devices for sampling water and steam, made of  stainless steel.
The HRSG design provides for the possibility of  maintaining it in a hot standby.
The HRSG is supplied in blocks. The design of  the HRSG provides installation both with supply blocks and with mounting blocks with their enlargement at the construction site.
The design of the HRSG and the delivery  blockiness of its units  was  developed taking into account the technology of  manufacturing, transportation, installation, repair and operation.
The supply of  HRSG is carried out in prefabricated blocks of maximum overall dimensions and maximum factory completeness of parts, based on the conditions of loading and unloading operations, transportation and storage. Coefficient of delivery blockiness is not less than 80% of  the calculated mass ofHRSG.

To  ensure explosion  and fire safety during the operation of gas  turbine power plants,  gas-air paths,  including gas ducts and a HRSG, must be ventilated  (ventilated)  for at least 5  minutes before ignition of the GT burners. In order to ensure a quick start-up of the GT, it is allowed to ventilate the gas-air path in advance during the shutdown process during the GT rotor coastdown by turning on the starter. In this case, the GT must be equipped with a system that excludes the penetration of fuel gas into the gas-air path when the GT is in standby, by locking the gas pipeline with air at a pressure higher than the pressure of the fuel gas in the gas pipeline. The control of the state «GT and gas ducts are purged» when the GT is in reserve should be carried out by the pressure difference between the shut-off air and fuel gas in the gas pipeline before the shut-off valve.

Relay protection is provided in the scope corresponding to the current « Rules for the installation of  electrical installations» (RIEi) and «Guidelines for relay protection».  Relay protection of  the main circuit elements is provided using microprocessor devices.
Relay  protection  of the  main  equipment  (generator-transformer  units,  reserve  transformers, 220kV connections) is provided in the form of  two mutually redundant autonomous protection systems («Main»  and  «Reserve»  protection).  The  composition  of the  protections  is  determined  by  the requirements  of the  «Electrical  Installation  Rules»  and  the  electrical  equipment  developer.  The distribution of protection  by sets is  carried  out on the basis of  the principle of interchangeability  of protection systems with redundancy for the main most probable and most severe damage. For each set of  protections, individual measuring transformers, separate circuits for direct operating current, separate input and output circuits,  as well as signaling  circuits  are provided.  Each of  the sets of  protections is made  on  the  basis  of  digital protection,  implemented  on  the microprocessor  principle.  Each microprocessor terminal provides the possibility of  indicating electrical quantities, setting parameters and entering protection settings, with the indicated values displayed on the monitor screen of  the external human-machine interface  or on the liquid crystal  display of  the terminal.  The  terminals  provide the ability to communicate with external digital devices via independent, galvanically isolated channels.
The ASG 6kV part provides for the installation of  CSG with microprocessor relay blocks. The ASG 6kV is equipped with fast-acting protection against arc  faults inside ASG,  logical protection of busbars and operational blocking, preventing the possibility of  erroneous operations with disconnectors, grounding knives, withdrawable carts of  PSG.

If  buildings and structures have straight and vented pipes for free removal of  gases and vapors of  explosive concentration into the atmosphere, the area of  protection of  lightning rods should include the space above the edge of  the pipes, in accordance with Section 9 of en PK 2.04-103-2013 (SP RK 2.04-103-2013).

To  monitor  the  perimeter  fences  and  gates,  a  video  surveillance  system  (CCTV)  should  be provided. Fixed-position cameras with fixed focal length lenses and pan-tilt zoom (PTZ) cameras should be used to provide  adequate coverage.  Remote control of PTZ  cameras should be provided.  Camera systems must be digital systems that must be user-configurable, scale, use digital storage devices, and be distributed over large networks.
It must be connected to an intrusion detection system and provide automatic calling of cameras in response to an alarm.
The Contractor shall be responsible for designing and placing CCTV cameras at strategic points, mounted on buildings or using masts, as required, to achieve full coverage of  the required areas.
The video surveillance system must be a high quality, high performance networked digital video surveillance  system  and  must  be  designed  so  that  people  can  be clearly  seen  anywhere  within  the coverage area. CCTV images displayed on monitors or retrieved from storage must be clear enough to allow clear and unambiguous identification of people and vehicles.
Solid-state  surveillance  cameras  using  charge-coupled  devices  (CCDs)  capable  of providing maximum resolution, high-definition color video images should be provided. Cameras must be wide dynamic range (WDR).  Cameras installed in locations subject to changes in light levels should have lenses equipped with automatic iris adjustment.
A digital  storage system shall be provided capable of storing video surveillance images in a compressed time-lapse format or in real-time as needed. Images should usually be stored in timelapse mode. The storage system must provide redundant storage elements to ensure that data is not lost in the event of  a storage element failure. Storage capacity must be at least 72 hours, with some cameras running in slow motion mode and the rest of the cameras running continuously.  An alarm should sound when the  storage  capacity  reaches  80  percent. The lower level  is  the  input-output  level  of information  (Input/Output Level)  - remote data collection  modules  (devices  for  communication  with  the  object  DCO  modules)  from  process parameters sensors, primary converters, actuators, regulatory bodies, provides the main functions of  the system for collecting information and issuance of control actions on actuators and consists of signal input / output stations, cabinets of industrial intermediate relay and terminal blocks.

Technological equipment sensors are used to convert the measured physical quantities into an electrical analog signal, which is fed into the system through cable connections.
The plant  control  system APCS should be the main and, if possible, the only (basic) control system used throughout the enterprise. However, it is recognized that certain areas of  the plant may be provided  by  sub-suppliers  who  provide  their  own  control  systems.  In  such  circumstances,  these subsystems must be connected through redundant interfaces so that the operators of the MCP are fully informed and can control the entire installation, all installations and objects.
The overall design of the system should be provided by a fully integrated plant management system  to  control,  manage,  display,  signal  and  record  selected  physical  and  electrical  parameters associated with all areas of the plant.
The APCS system will have a functionally and geographically distributed architecture using a number of  independent BCPs containing control processors, power supplies, data transmission systems, cross-connect and terminal devices. The BCP must be capable of  autonomous operation and perform the functions of data  acquisition,  calculation,  open  loop  and feedback control.  Communication between nodes located in different areas of the station and operator or engineer workstations located in central control  rooms and local  control rooms should be carried out over properly designed redundant high­ speed serial data lines. The communication system must be designed so that rate variables are updated and  control  commands  are  issued  without  compromising  system  performance.  The  communication system must include all control equipment, error correction and cabling.
The normal operation of  the station, including start-up, load changes, shutdown, monitoring, etc., must be carried out from the MCP through the operator's workstations.
The APCS should be designed to provide maximum availability by including built-in redundancy in  both  hardware  and  software.  This  should  include  redundant  control  processors,  a  data  highway, input/output modules as needed, and power supplies with automatic failover to a standby unit when a fault or failure of  the operating unit is detected. Redundancy must be provided for input/output modules used for safety-related control or protection functions.

In  particular,  the  redundant  control  processors  will  be  able  to  failover  without changing station state, sequence state, or control actions at any point in the station's operation.
Comprehensive system diagnostics should be included in the APCS to assist with maintenance and  troubleshooting. These diagnostic systems should, at a minimum, cover memory, control processors, input/output cards, data highway, and storage devices. System maintenance software must be provided.

The  MCP will be the control center of  the Site, so it must be ergonomic and aesthetically pleasing to ensure that the operator's working conditions are of  a high standard, providing a safe and comfortable working  environment  for station  personnel  and  allowing  them to work  efficiently. A  set  of graphic  displays  at  the  workstations  of the  APCS  operators  is  the  main  means  of presenting  information  and  managing  the  Facility.  Graphic  displays  should  provide  operators  with dynamic information about the process and provide a picture of  the plant based on piping and IA.
Graphic displays  should  form an associated hierarchical  structure  consisting  of a number of different graphic display formats, as follows:
- plant overview - displays the overall schedule of  the plant, showing production, consumption, and the main parameters of  the plant.
- system overview - to display detailed information about the system or systems, as well as to display the status of  the main equipment.
- system area - to display all installation elements and process parameters for the area/process in question.
- plant elements - to display all the details of  the plant element process (  can be displayed in «pop­ up windows»).
- faceplates - these graphics shall display the control faceplates for a plant element, system or group of systems on the same graphics.
- trends - to display historical data graphs.
- bar graph - these displays show data values relative to each other (for example, generator stator temperatures).
- menu graphics - they should display a list of  system or systems graphics.
- text graphics - these should display ready-to-run lists or help screens.
Graphics should contain only those details that are necessary for the operator to determine the condition of the equipment at a glance.
Graphic  displays  must  be  connected  through  «hotspots»  that  connect  the  graphics  as  a continuation of  the process. Hot spots should be highlighted with text describing the continuation of  the process.
The design of graphic displays should be concise, uniform in structure,  unambiguous, and use reports.
The APCS must be capable of presenting operator-defined and user-configurable reports to the operator.  The information in reports can be either in tabular form or in pre-formatted report form and can be automatic at specific times or on demand. Reports should include, at a minimum, periodic logs, daily logs and  group logs, alarm summary  log,  sequence of events log,  post-shutdown analysis logs, system  status/failures,  energy balance  and  efficiency  log,  etc.  comply  with  the  requirements  of the Competent authority and environmental permit. The  function  «Registration  of  emergency  situations»  (RES)  should  be  provided  for  the accumulation  and  presentation  on  screens  and  (or)  printing  of data  on  the  process  of occurrence, development  and  elimination  of emergency  situations  with  reference  to  astronomical  time  with  an accuracy of 1  ms. The RES function should ensure the registration of, as a rule, reliable technological data for  the period preceding  the  accident  and after its  occurrence,  on the operation of the main and auxiliary equipment, the operation of protections, interlocks, automatic control devices and personnel.
All information involved in the RES is conditionally divided into three groups:
- A - analog and discrete signals characterizing the state of control objects, the registration cycle of  which corresponds to the cycle of  updating information on monitor screens;
- B - analog and discrete signals characterizing the state of  control objects that require registration with high resolution;
- C - initiative signals for the operation of electrical and technological protections, event signals associated  with  the  impact  of personnel on control  objects,  which are  also  subject to the  actions  of technological and electrical protections, event signals associated with the output of analog parameters beyond  the  alarm settings  or  operation of protections,  and also  the  values  of analog  parameters  for electrical equipment that require registration with super high resolution.
It is necessary to have recorders of  different time characteristics for: - thermal power equipment; -electrical equipment; - electrical equipment associated with the receipt of  signals from AEA.
It is advisable to have several (the number corresponds to the purpose of  the project) independent registrars of emergency situations (ES) in the HSC for units and assemblies.  The recorders can work simultaneously and independently and  record  arbitrary  sets  of parameters  spe�ified  at  the  stages  of development and operation of the system.
The following enlarged RES algorithm should be provided. Prior to the arrival of a signal about the  beginning  of an  emergency,  there  should  be  a  constant  sliding  accumulation of data in  the  pre­ emergency interval. When an initiating signal characterizing an accident appears, all the accumulated data are «frozen» and the process of registering the development and localization of the accident in the post-accident interval begins.
The RES function should not take into account the real states of  the protections (  enabled, enabled in the information mode - signaled). Recorders in the mode of  post-emergency recording of information should not be switched if the triggered protection is signaled.
The imitation of the beginning of the ES is provided to check the functionality of the function when testing the equipment.
Information about the accident is recorded in the archive.

To ensure fire and explosion safety, there must be:
- measures were taken to minimize the risk of fires and an effective system for their detection and extinguishing was organized.
- ACS requirements have been established and implemented to avoid hazardous conditions (in terms of rotational speeds, temperatures, vibrations, etc.).
- an alarm system is organized to alert about dangerous, unsafe conditions and an emergency shutdown of the GT to protect personnel and (or) equipment.
- the  placement of units and systems in accordance with a certain category of production in separate compartments with equipment for the corresponding purpose was carried out;
- door closers and a system for monitoring the open position of doors in the GT shelter were installed.
The  requirements  for  explosion  and  fire  safety  in  accordance  with  fOCT 12.1.010  (GOST 12.1.010) and fOCT 12.1.004 (GOST 12.1.004) must be met
The electrical equipment  of the  GT  for  electrical  safety  must  comply with  fOCT  12.1.019 (GOST 12.1.019), rOCT 12.1.030 (GOST 12.1.030), rOCT 12.1.038 (GOST 12.1.038) and rOCT P 51330.0 (GOST R 51330.0).
The fire protection system shall include, as a minimum, a fire extinguishing system, fire detection and combustible gas detection systems.
When a fire or the presence of fuel gas in the air is detected, the emergency protection system should automatically turn off  the GT by direct action on the shut-off  fuel valve.
The fire extinguishing system must be switched on automatically. Switching on is duplicated manually by buttons located on the outside of both sides of the casing of the units controlled by the fire alarm.
Do not use halogens or other ozone-destroying gases for extinguishing.
The inlets and outlets in the ventilation and sealing system must be equipped with valves. Their closure during fires keeps the medium supplied for extinguishing inside the shelter.
If the GT is installed under the shell and operates on gaseous fuel or in gas hazardous areas, the sequence of automatically performed operations at start-up includes purging and checking the safety (presence of gas) under the shell. Only after purging and signaling that there is no fuel gas under the casing,  electrical  equipment  located  in  the  hazardous  area  can  be  energized.  In  the  presence  of continuous purges  and control  of at  least  10  air exchanges per minute, the explosive category of the volume under the skin can be reduced by 1.

The Facility's control systems must be designed with adequate software and hardware protection against the threats of  cyber attacks and industrial sabotage. Control systems in this case refer to electronic
or microprocessor systems that use software-based programs for their main operation, including, but not limited to, APCS, PLCs, and proprietary control systems.
Attacks are often carried out through malicious software and firmware (malware) introduced in a variety of  ways, including:

- On the Internet.

Continuous  management  and continuous improvement  must  be  applied  to  ensure  ongoing  protection,  with  threat  awareness  and response being important factors.

Technological protections form control actions on the executive bodies (actuators and switching devices) in order to protect personnel, prevent damage to equipment and localize the consequences of accidents. Protections have the highest priority in relation to other discrete actions.
The shutdown of the  active action of the protections and their  output «on/off the  signal» are carried out by  the  maintenance personnel  with  the  approval of the  management by  non-operational means separately for each protection.
In the event of simultaneous operation of protections that cause a different degree of unloading of  the equipment, priority is given to protection of a stronger action (with deeper unloading).
The action of the protections is maintained for a time sufficient to perform the longest control operation.
Protections  are  entered  (and  removed)  automatically  when  the  specified  conditions  appear (disappear).  After  entering  the  protection  work  continuously.  The  fact of input/output  protection  is signaled and logged. Information on protections that have not been put into operation is also logged and issued for signaling.  An authorized manual  input-output of protections is provided at the request of operational personnel, and separately for each protection, with the obligatory fixation of  this event in the archive.
The action of  the protections is unilateral: changing the composition of  the operating equipment, the state of the control objects and putting the  equipment into operation  after it is turned off by the protection is carried out by the operating personnel after the elimination of the causes that caused the protection to operate.
The operation of the protections is accompanied by light and sound alarms and the activation of RES. Protections operating with a time delay of more than 5 s have an indication of the start of work. HSC provides an opportunity to test each of the protections on the stopped equipment. Changes in the technological protection settings are made by service personnel with access authorization, recorded in the archive and accompanied by mandatory logging.

Flow meters operating on the principles of  differential pressure must be designed in accordance with the requirements:  ISO 5167, CT PK 2.69-2004 (ST RK 2.69-2004), CT PK 2.131-2013 (ST RK 2.131-2013), fOCT 8.586.1-2005 (GOST 8.586.1-2005), rocT 8.586.2-2005 (GOST 8.586.2-2005), fOCT 8.586.3-2005 (GOST 8.586.3-2005), fOCT 8.586.4-2005 (GOST 8.586.4-2005), fOCT 8.586.52005 (GOST 8.586.5-2005),
- turbine flow meters - in accordance with  ISO 9951, CT PK 2547-2014 (ST RK 2547-2014),
- ultrasonic flow meters - in accordance with  ISO 17089, CT PK 2549-2014 (ST RK 2549-2014).
For high pressure  applications  above 25 barg. The primary device holder must be made of a material similar to that of the pipeline in which it  is  to be  installed  and must be butt-welded to  the pipeline.  In other cases, flange connections should be used whenever possible. For line sizes less than 50mm, a precision pipe assembly with a minimum line  size of 50mm should be used. All differential pressure  devices  must  be  fitted  with  draw-off shut-off valves  and  drain  valves  or  two-way  valve manifolds, if  required. All differential pressure devices must be supplied with individual calibration data.
Multiple measurements of  the same flow may be taken from the same orifice or venturi, but must be made through separate sampling points, parallel connections from the same sampling point are not allowed.
The flowmeters must in all cases comply with the process conditions applicable to the place of measurement and the environment in which they are installed. Meters used for energy, tariff, or metering purposes must be supplied with adjacent piping where necessary, with a calibration certificate from an approved laboratory. Piston flowmeters must be accurate within 0.25%.
If density, temperature, or pressure corrections are required for tariff or capacity control signals, then such measurements must be made near the location of  the flowmeter.

The temperature measurement method used must be selected for the specific application, taking into account the requirements for accuracy and reliability.
Sensitive  elements  for  measuring  the  temperature  of air,  inert  gases  and  radiation  must  be equipped  with  an  appropriate  protective  sheath.  For  steam,  water  and  hazardous  applications, thermowells must be used. If temperature sensors are to be installed in jacketed pipes and apparatuses, extensions must be fitted with protective covers to allow access to the sensor's connection head and outside  the  jacket.  The  connecting  heads  of the  sensitive  elements  must  be  located  at  an  ambient temperature not exceeding 50 ° C and be waterproof
The thermowells must be suitable for the pipeline in which they are installed and for the physical conditions of  the parameter to be measured at the place of  installation. Thermo  wells for steam and feed water must be weldable in place. Test thermowells shall be provided with a cover.
Resistance thermometer detectors  (RTDs)  should  only  be  used if they can be  easily  replaced without loss of  plant performance. RTDs must comply with IEC 60751, [OCT 13384-93 (GOST 1338493) using three-wire connections for applications up to 450 ° C. Resistive sensors shall be single element or  dual  element  as  specified  in  accordance  with  the  Customer's  requirements,  Part  4,  Tab  34  Mechanical Diagrams.  Resistive  sensors  must  be  fitted  with  waterproof heads  with  terminal  blocks designed to prevent the ingress of  all foreign matter and liquids. When measuring temperature difference, use an  RTD in accordance  with  IEC  60751  Grade  I,  fOCT  6651-2009 (GOST  6651-2009),  fOCT 13384-93 (GOST 13384-93).
Locally installed signal converters must be provided for all RTD and thermocouple measuring devices.  Preferably,  they are  located  at  the head  of the  measuring  device  or,  alternatively,  in a local junction box, if required by local environmental conditions. The transmitters must provide a 4-20 mA linear  output  for  further  transmission  to  the  control  system  or monitoring  equipment.  If necessary, linearization and cold junction compensation must be enabled.
Thermocouples must be used in accordance with the requirements of IEC 60584, [OCT 661694 (GOST 6616-94), [OCT 6651-2009 (GOST 6651-2009). Special attention must be paid to the design and  installation  of  thermocouple systems  to ensure that inaccuracies  are not introduced  into measurements  due  to  the  use of  unsuitable materials or incorrect installation. Cold  junction compensation must be provided, as well as compensation cables of appropriate size and material where necessary. In addition to GT and ST, thermocouples must be installed on the basic equipment in such a way that they can be replaced during the operation of  the plant.

Position measuring devices or switches (e.g. limit switches, proximity switches, etc.) must either be located away from sources of heat or process gases or liquids, or must be appropriately classified for this environment. Where vibration-free locations are not possible, the mounting device must provide flexibility in the connection between the device, the measuring point and the transmitter mountings.
Position  switches  associated  with the  GT  control  system must have two-pole  single-position contacts. All other position switches shall have, as a minimum, isolated two-pole, two-position contacts and be such that, under normal process operating conditions, the contacts in the switch will close, unless otherwise approved by the Customer. If  necessary, the switches should have adjustable settings.
For  encoders  in high  temperature  environments,  calibration  of encoders  and  setting  of limit switches should not be affected by high/low operating temperatures during startup and shutdown.
As  a  general  rule,  the  switch  contacts  must  be  fully  protected  from  adverse  environmental influences, such  as  dust,  moisture,  corrosive  materials,  etc.,  and  the  contact  closure  must  be instantaneous by clicking. Switches must be of  a robust design to withstand vibration and shock due to the movement of actuators, etc., and wire-break monitoring must be provided.
As an alternative to limit switches, solid-state proximity switches are acceptable.
In addition to the GT and ST on the base equipment, valves and dampers with position feedback should be used for position feedback RVDTs  (Rotary Variable Differential  Transformers) or LVDTs (Linear Variable Differential Transformers). It must be possible to adjust the 0 percent valve or damper position and adjust the RVDT  /L  VDT range so that a 100 percent RVDT  /L  VDT position corresponds to a  100 percent valve or damper position. The RVDT/LVDT output must be 4-20mA or a digital signal for 0-100% travel to connect to a control system.

Quality instruments that monitor the chemical or physicm al properties of process fluids and substances can either be installed directly in the process line or vessel, or use a sampling system. Sensors should be of robust construction and not require frequent maintenance or recalibration. If the sensors require the use of calibration solutions or gases, a minimum of one year's supply must be maintained under normal  use.  If sensors  need  to be  replaced  or removed for recalibration or upgrade at  regular intervals, sufficient replacement sensors should be supplied for one year of normal use.
Quality measuring instruments should be selected for continuous, infrequent or continuously discontinuous operation as appropriate for the measurement and intended application.
Analyzers should be selected with regard to the accuracy, reliability and maintenance frequency of  the individual devices. Wherever possible, analyzers should use a sensor for on-line analysis.
Sampling systems should include, as appropriate, the sensors, valves, filters, coolers, pressure regulators,  coalescers,  flowmeters,  sampling  devices,  pipe  fittings,  and  pumps necessary  to  provide analyzers  with  a  representative  and  properly  conditioned  sample.  The  time  delay between taking  a sample from a process and making the result available to the analyzer should be appropriate for the measurement  and  control  requirements  of the  particular  process.  The  preferred  method  of keeping sampling delays within acceptable limits is to place the analyzer close to the sampling point. If this is not practicable, the  lag  of the  sampling system from the speed of the  distance should be  reduced by increasing the  speed of the sample.  The  sample must be returned to the  process or disposed of in  an economical and safe manner.
Where  practicable,  prefabricated  analyzer  racks  should  be  provided  and  should  include  all necessary sample coolers,  analyzers,  air,  electrical and cooling water distribution systems, and  pre­ assembled accessories. Such devices should allow testing of  the entire assembly prior to shipment to the site and  should  be capable of being  conveniently disconnected from  real-time operation to facilitate scheduled maintenance and calibration.
Arrangements  should  also  include  the  collection  of used  samples  and their  safe  disposal at appropriate disposal points. Emissions of flammable vapors, including sampling lines, must be vented

The vibration control and protection system of GT should be based on seismic and non-contact sensors according to the manufacturer's standard.
All  other vibration measurements should be  performed on all large rotating or reciprocating machines for protection and condition monitoring. Processing equipment must be provided to power, detect and display vibration data for each measurement point and must be available to the APCS. Each measurement  must  be  accompanied by  an  appropriate  alarm  if high  levels  of vibration could cause damage or affect the safety of the installation.
Vibration monitoring systems must comply with the requirements of ISO 7919 and ISO 10816, CT PK rOCT P HCO 13373-1-2011 (ST RK GOST RISO 13373-1-2011), rocT ISO 20806-2013 (GOST ISO 20806-2013  ). Where possible, standardization and interchangeability of  components should be implemented.
Vibration measuring devices should be of  the non-contact transducer type and should be designed and selected to operate under the specific intended conditions. Vibration sensors should be located on or near each machine bearing, mounted in threaded holes in the bearing housing or on a rigid bracket.
Relative vibration should be measured with non-contact sensors (non-contact type) to measure the relative motion between the shaft and the bearing housing. To measure the relative vibration of a shaft, two sensors mounted radially in the same transverse plane, perpendicular to the shaft axis and at an angle of 90 ° to each other, should be used. A key phase shifter (sensor of one pulse per revolution) must also be provided for each shaft.
Absolute  vibration  should  be  measured  with  non-contact  sensors  measuring  relative  shaft vibration in combination  with a seismic sensor (velocity sensor or accelerometer) measuring support vibration. Both transducers must be mounted close to each other so that they make the same absolute movement in the measurement direction. Their conditioned outputs must be vector summed to provide a measurement of the absolute motion of  the shaft.
Measurement  of both  relative  and  absolute  shaft  vibration  must  be  made  on  the  board  to adequately cover the frequency spectrum of  the machine.
Vibration switches must be sensitive to low-frequency vibrations associated with unbalance in the mass of machines. Switches must be insensitive to high frequency vibration, external shocks, etc. acting on the machine. The switch must respond to vibrations from any direction. Switch action must be latched and must be reset manually or, if  indicated, electrically by means of  a solenoid. The setting must be adjustable. Switches should be set to allow easy access for reset and calibration.

Valves and dampers that must operate during start-up, shutdown and normal operation of the plant must be actuated.
Actuators  for  control valves  and  dampers  should  normally  be  of the  pneumatic,  electric  or hydraulic type. Actuators for ON/OFF, shutdown or manual positioning of units should normally be electrical. Other types of  drives for specific applications in accordance with safety requirements or other technological requirements must be approved by the Customer.
The failure response of all actuators in the event of loss of the prime mover (air pressure, oil pressure, power supply) must be in a safe/predetermined position, which must be indicated on the piping and instrumentation diagrams (piping diagram), schedule valve, etc. d.
If the actuator is required to control position, an actuator position feedback and indication must be provided that is independent of  the position request signal. The open and closed positions of all other valves controlled by the actuator must be controlled through the APCS for indication to the CCR.
Where the control requirement requires split range or non-linear operation, the split or non-linear range ca1culation must be performed external to the drive in such a way that standard drive input signals are supported.
In addition to the basic GT and ST equipment, all actuators must have a manual control device (to operate the valve in the event of  a failure of  the prime mover) and a mechanically operated indicator showing the true position of  the valve.

chunks.text:
Control  valves  must  be  supplied  with  appropriate  actuators  that  meet  the  operational  and environmental requirements of the plant. All actuators must be provided with local controls that can be used without the use of tools. The operator must be warned of the loss of remote/automatic control of the actuator valve.
All control drives must have local and remote (in the CCR via APCS) indication of the actual position of  the valve. For remote control or indication purposes, an appropriate position transmitter must be provided  (  eg  based  on  a differential transducer with a  linear variable characteristic).  Where  it is necessary to provide only a limited number of  discrete position indications, position switches should be used. Switch settings must be adjustable.
All  drives  must  be  designed  for  heavy-duty  operation  and  withstand  the  maximum  drive capability. Actuators must be equipped with stroke and torque limiting switches for blocking and control functions, as well as to provide remote indication to the APCS. Actuators may have electronic torque control instead of torque switches. Actuators that will not be damaged when full power is applied in a permanently locked position do not require torque switches.
label: text

chunks.text:
Valves with electric actuator shall consist of self-contained actuator units with motor, gearbox, contactor, controls, limit/torque switches and all ancillary equipment installed in each actuator housing. If necessary,  anti-condensation  heaters  should  be  provided.  Drives  using  frequency  converters  and power  electronics  instead  of  contactors  are  also  permitted.  A  lockable  local/remote  switch  with open/close  controls  must  be  located  on  the  actuator.  With  the  exception  of the  basic  GT  and  ST equipment, the actuators must be designed so that they can be disconnected from the valve in the event of a malfunction and the valve operates normally with the handwheel.
The diameter of the flywheel and gear should be such that it can be operated by one person with minimal effort. A lockable mechanical clutch mechanism shall be provided to prevent power control of the actuators while operating the helm.
Each end of the drive stroke must be equipped with suitable limit and torque switches to prevent excessive stroke and subsequent damage to the valve or actuator. Limit switches must also be installed to provide remote (in the CCR via APCS) indication of valve position. The actuator must be provided with a local valve position indication.  The relationship between the command signal and the actuator position must be controlled and any discrepancy must be signaled to the APCS.
The drive motors must be suitable for use on a 400 V, 3  phase, 50 Hz network and, as far as possible, must be obtained from a single manufacturer, to be agreed with the Customer.
The  drive  motors  must  be  equipped,  if necessary,  with  a  thermal  protection  device.  Torque switches or electronic torque control shall be provided to control the motor in the fully closed position and,  if necessary,  to  protect the  motor  in the open position.  Torque switches must be independently adjustable and adjustable for each position.  Electric actuators must be provided with means of local manual control.
label: text

chunks.text:
Pneumatic  actuators/positioners  must  be  supplied  in  accordance  with  the  operational  and environmental requirements of the valve or actuator assembly. Pneumatic actuators/positioners must be capable of actuating the  valve or  driven unit through its full stroke at  a signal between 0.2 and  1  bar using any of  the following:
- pneumatic signal directly to the drive;
- pneumatic signal directly to the positioner;
- electrical signal to the electro-pneumatic converter;
- electrical signal to the solenoid control valve.
Pneumatic actuators and  actuator units shall  automatically return to a fail-safe/predetermined position  upon  signal  and/or  air  failure,  unless  process  or  specification  or  detailed  engineering requirements call for a «stay in place» response.
Where necessary, «lock-out» devices shall be provided to ensure that the actuator remains in the operating position prevailing just prior to the air failure.
All pneumatic control  equipment, control actuators and control valves should  operate satisfactorily at a normal air supply pressure of approximately 7 barg, but not less than 5.5 barg.
Volume boosters should be provided on hinges where quick response (  eg pressure) is required to improve stability.
All positioners and electropneumatic converters must be equipped with three pressure gauges, air supply, signal input and control air output, and an air filter-regulator kit with lubricating oil.
For GT, ST and their auxiliaries,  the valve position must be provided by the LVDT, all other position sensors and limit switches must be provided for remote indication of  the valve positions in the CCR through  the  APCS.  Position  measuring  systems  using  potentiometers  must  not  be  used.  All feedback switching signals must come from voltage-free contacts.
If  an electropneumatic converter precedes or is an integral part of the positioner, measures shall be provided for connecting portable test equipment to provide electrical references or pulses to enable the actuator to stroke for testing purposes.

The units offered are to be self-contained, fully sealed, allowing the entire unit to be moved to a clean room for any maintenance requirement.
Devices accepting either 4-20 mA signals or pulse input signals are allowed.
Failure of the internal hydraulic supply should cause the actuator to lock in its last operating position or move to a fail-safe position and give the appropriate alarm to the CCR.

Solenoid  valves  must be  selected  based on the  type  of process  fluid,  the  temperature  of the environment in which the valve operates, and the frequency of operation. For applications other than air use, the solenoid must be designed to be protected from the process environment.
Solenoid housings must be waterproof. The solenoid coils must be insulated class H.
The open/closed state of the solenoid valve must be transferred to the APCS.
Solenoids  should  normally  be  operated  at  24V  of direct  current  and  48V  of direct  current. However, the Contractor may offer 110 V of direct current in places where voltage drops are expected due to longer connection cables.
label: text

chunks.text: Critical manual valves important to the process must have their open/closed state monitored and displayed to the CCR via the APCS. In such cases, limit switches must be provided at each end of the stroke.
label: text

chunks.text: All control and I&A cables supplied under this contract shall comply with the latest applicable IEC standards. I&A cables (  other than fiber optic cables) and electrical wiring must have stranded copper conductors,  thermoplastic  insulation,  and  a  thermoplastic  outer  sheath.  Protection  against  pests  and insects  must  be  provided.  When  laying  outside  buildings  and  fences  and  in  the  absence  of general mechanical  protection,  the  cables  must  be  armored  from  galvanized  steel  wire  with  a  waterproof thermoplastic sheath. All methods of mechanical protection, except for steel wire armor, belong to the Customer. Cables laid in cable trays, ladders, troughs and conduits do not require mechanical protection.
label: text

chunks.text:
Each piece of equipment must be labeled in a cohesive, durable and legible manner, indicating the  purpose,  the  identification  number  of the  installation  and,  if necessary,  the  functions  of any workplace.  Labels  must  be on  the  front  and  rear  entrance  doors  of all  cells.  Labels  should  also  be provided inside cabinets to help identify equipment and terminals. Instruments, valves, actuators, and all other field-installed equipment must be similarly labeled.
All label material and dimensions, legend and printing method must be approved. Surfaces of plates for cabinets and instrumentation should be matte or satin to avoid glare. Colors must be durable and not fade. The labels must be secured with stainless steel screws. Any alternative fastening method is subject to approval.
Hazard signs must have red letters on a white background and comply with BS EN 60073 and rocT 12.4.026-2015 (GOST 12.4.026-2015).
Cables, conductors and pairs must be uniquely identified using a consistent system.
Each cable must be marked with a cable number approved by the Customer.
Each core of the cable must be uniquely identified using plastic lock ring lugs or similar means. «Clip on» or «c» type tips should not be used. The main identifier must be approved by the Customer.
label: text

chunks.text:
All de-energized metal parts of the plant, equipment, components, enclosures, racks, etc. must be  earthed  by connecting  to  the  main  earth  bus  in  an approved  manner,  and  all  earth  terminals  and connections must be properly sized.
Grounding must comply with the relevant sections of BS 6739, BS 7671, IEEE 80, IEEE 665 and IEEE 1050  or equivalent  international  standards and norms, the requirement of the Republic of Kazakhstan rOCT 12.1.030-81 (GOST 12.1.030-81), Order of the Minister of Energy of the Republic of Kazakhstan dated March 20, 2015 No. 230 «On approval of  the Rules for the installation of electrical installations» (RIEi).
The  Contractor  shall  prepare  a  document  on  the  principles  of  I&A  grounding  prior  to commencement of the grounding design. This earthing concept is subject to customer approval.
Protective screens around insulated cables must be isolated from field devices connected through any field  junction  boxes  and  be  continuous  to  an  earth  point  in the  cubicle  or  destination  panel.  If c·ontinuous shields are required to provide protection against interference, precautions must be taken to ensure  that potentially severe ground faults cannot damage the cable or equipment. The cable armor should only be earthed for electrical safety and not for noise reduction. The cable armor must be insulated from the cable shields and must be connected to site ground at one point.
If  the Contractor's project requires a separate and special earthing device (for example, a «clean» earth for electronic equipment), then the Contractor shall provide such means of earthing as necessary. If  such earthing systems require a single connection of  the I&A equipment to the plant's main earth bus, then a detachable jumper shall be provided to connect the equipment's earth to the plant's main earth bus for testing purposes. This detachable link must be clearly marked with a warning symbol. All clean earth rods of the instrument must also be appropriately marked.
Any separate  ground  bar  for measuring circuits  should  be  located  at  the bottom of racks  or equipment panels and consist of  a solid copper rod 6 mm thick and 25 mm wide (length according to the size of the panel), with holes and threads for screw terminals and wire lugs. This ground bus must be isolated from the chassis and equipment ground.
All panels, cabinet doors or swing frames must use a flexible cable or braid to ground these elements; door hinges should not be used as a means of  grounding this piece of equipment.
label: text

chunks.text: An integrated  security system for the entire  plant shall be installed to control and monitor all access to and from the Site. The security system should consist of  video surveillance, intrusion detection and access control systems. These systems should provide security personnel at the gate and operator personnel in the central control room with the means to monitor and control activities within the plant boundaries, as well as to view the plant's external fencing, gates and critical areas of the facility from control desks and color television monitors.
label: text

chunks.text:
To  monitor  the  perimeter  fences  and  gates,  a  video  surveillance  system  (CCTV)  should  be provided. Fixed-position cameras with fixed focal length lenses and pan-tilt zoom (PTZ) cameras should be used to provide  adequate coverage. Remote control of PTZ cameras should be provided.  Camera systems must be digital systems that must be user-configurable, scale, use digital storage devices, and be distributed over large networks.
It must be connected to an intrusion detection system and provide automatic calling of  cameras in response to an alarm.
The Contractor shall be responsible for designing and placing CCTV cameras at strategic points, mounted on buildings or using masts, as required, to achieve full coverage of  the required areas.
The video surveillance system must be a high quality, high performance networked digital video surveillance  system  and  must  be  designed  so  that  people  can be  clearly  seen  anywhere  within  the coverage area. CCTV images displayed on monitors or retrieved from storage must be clear enough to allow clear and unambiguous identification of people and vehicles.
Solid-state  surveillance  cameras  using  charge-coupled devices  (CCDs)  capable  of providing maximum resolution, high-definition color video images should be provided. Cameras must be wide dynamic range (WDR). Cameras installed in locations subject to changes in light levels should have lenses equipped with automatic iris adjustment.
A digital storage system shall be provided  capable  of storing video surveillance images  in a compressed time-lapse format or in real-time as needed. Images should usually be stored in timelapse mode. The storage system must provide redundant storage elements to ensure that data is not lost in the event of  a storage element failure. Storage capacity must be at least 72 hours, with some cameras running in slow motion mode and the rest of the cameras running continuously. An alarm should sound when the  storage  capacity  reaches  80  percent.  The  video  surveillance  system  must  comply  with  the requirements: Decree of the  Government of the Republic of Kazakhstan dated May 6, 2021  No.  305. «On approval of requirements for the organization of anti-terrorist protection of objects vulnerable to terrorists.» In case of  failure of the storage element, the transition to the backup storage element should be automatic. The storage system must have the means to overlay the camera number and date/time onto the images.
Color television monitors capable of  displaying any of  the system's cameras should be provided. Monitors and controllers will be located both in the CCR and in the security service premises.
label: text

chunks.text: An electronic intrusion detection system is to be supplied as part of the Contract for perimeter fencing and entry gates to the Site. The detection system must detect and alarm when any perimeter fence is tampered with or entered.  When an alarm condition occurs, security lighting in the area and surrounding areas should be turned on, and camera images in the area and surrounding areas should be displayed and recorded automatically. The intrusion detection system should notify security personnel and operatives of  an attempt to enter the station through a protective fence.
label: text

chunks.text: An access control system to the facility should be provided that covers all access points to the facility.  The  access control system to the site  should consist of automatic gates, an electronic access control system, an intercom between the gate and the CCR/gatehouse, as well as gate controls from the CCR and gatehouse. CCTV cameras should be located at all access points to ensure clear identification of  people and vehicles.
label: text

- Ambient temperature.
- Atmospheric humidity.

Loudspeakers  must  be  supplied  according  to  the  environmental  conditions  and  must  be positioned and oriented to provide the required sound coverage.
Power amplifiers must have sufficient power to power all loudspeakers under normal operating conditions plus a 20 percent overload margin.
The public address system shall include self-monitoring system to monitor the condition of  the public address equipment, including loudspeakers. Appropriate alarms should be given automatically to alert the operator when a malfunction is detected in the system.
The public address system must be powered by the UPS.
The facility's emergency evacuation alarm system should be integrated into the public address system to provide audible and visual indication throughout the facility and should block any other use of  the system.
label: text

chunks.text:
A factory siren/strobe system should be provided to alert CCGT personnel of an incident and report to predetermined locations. The siren system must be integrated with the public address system. When a siren is triggered, a certain tone should be played in the loudspeakers and beacons  should be turned  on to alert personnel in all rooms and areas  with a high level of noise in the enterprise. Sirens should have two tones, one for «alarm» and one for «all clear».
The  siren/strobe  system  must  be  supplied  and installed  in accordance with  NFP  A  and  other applicable  international standards.  The Contractor  shall  provide  sufficient sirens and  strobe  lights to cover the entire CCGT site, as well as all associated cabling, hardware and software.
It is the Contractor's responsibility to ensure that the sirens and strobes supplied are suitable for environmental conditions, and that the sirens are positioned and oriented to provide the required sound coverage. The number and location of  sirens must be such that the entire Facility is covered and approved by the Customer.
In places with a high level of  ambient noise, a stroboscopic lighting system should be provided. The  system  shall  include  a  self-monitoring  facility  to  monitor  the  condition  of equipment, including  sirens.  Appropriate  alarms  should  be  given  automatically  to  alert  the  operator  when  a malfunction is detected in the system.

An IT system shall be installed at the Facility to provide data communication for administrative purposes at the Facility, as well as communication between the Facility and the Customer's headquarters, and other locations.  The Contractor is responsible for providing cable infrastructure, data and power sockets in designated rooms and production areas, and all necessary network switches. The location of data  and  power  outlets,  as  well  as  cable  routes,  must  be  approved  by  the  Customer.  The  Internet connection  must  be secured through a hardware  firewall or similar  security device to protect the site network from unauthorized access.
A one-way Ethernet TCP/IP interface  must be provided with the APCS so that users of the station's LAN can view and access the process and operating data of the station from the APCS. This interface will be fully firewalled  from unauthorized access and to ensure complete security of station data on the APCS via PI or HTML.

The main tasks of the system are:
- 1) Monitoring of  the stress-strain state of structures and displacement of element points.
- 2) Monitoring of  the roll of the building and structure.
- 3) Monitoring of  natural oscillation frequency and damping decrement of the object.
- 4) Monitoring of foundation subsidence settlement.
- 5) Monitoring of  the level of seismic impact.

The materials selected by the Contractor shall be suitable for the respective application and shall last for the entire service life of  the power plant.
When choosing materials, the main consideration should be the compatibility of  materials and operating conditions. An important selection criterion should be the mechanical characteristics as well as the characteristics of  the materials related to workmanship and service (eg strength and weldability). The selected materials must be standardized and have convincingly proven their quality in the past.
The materials that make up those power plant components that will be in contact with water or subject to mechanical wear, including heat transfer surfaces, must be highly resistant to corrosion/erosion.
Inappropriate material combinations (eg carbon steel/stainless steel) should be avoided to prevent galvanic corrosion.
Asbestos  and  polychlorinated  diphenyl  (PCD)  containing  materials  and  persistent  organic pollutants (POPs) are not allowed to be used in the manufacture of  the power plant.

When implementing the project, the Contractor must comply with the requirements listed in the rules and regulations in force on the territory of the Republic of Kazakhstan.
All electrical equipment supplied must comply with the standards of the Republic of Kazakhstan in force for the period of execution of the Contract, unless the Customer has approved something else. Such  approval  will be given  only if the Contractor can convincingly demonstrate that the equipment complies with other generally accepted international standards and its quality is equivalent to the quality approved by the local standard. Installation must be carried out in accordance with appropriate standards and manufacturer's recommendations.
Electrical installation work must comply with the requirements of the relevant standards of the Republic of Kazakhstan, as well as the electrical equipment used in these areas.
The Contractor is responsible for providing the Customer with information that will be subject to regulatory review and assisting in obtaining the necessary licenses and approvals from the authorities for its scope of work, if such licenses and approvals are obtained on behalf of the Customer.
With  regard  to  the  main  and  auxiliary  equipment  operating  under  pressure,  the  regulatory documentation in force on the territory of the Republic of Kazakhstan is applied.
When preparing,  organizing  and  conducting  a  competition,  regulating  its  consequences,  it is necessary  to  be  guided  by  the  system  of  regulatory  legal  acts  and  regulatory  and  methodological documents in force in the Republic of Kazakhstan:
- -Decrees of the President of the Republic of Kazakhstan.
- -Laws of the Republic of Kazakhstan.
- -Decrees and Orders of the Government of the Republic of Kazakhstan.
- -State standards of the Republic of Kazakhstan (GOST).
- -Building codes and regulations, codes of practice and others.
The list of norms and standards in force at the time of signing the Contract is applied.
In the event that any norms, standards or rules contradict each other, the most stringent of them apply.
