It is necessary to provide that all mechanical, electrical and control equipment of the power plant, etc. provide free access for periodic maintenance throughout the life of the power plant.
When installing, both individual devices and devices related to equipment systems, it is necessary to be guided by the following main criteria:
- One worker in conditions of free access can lift a weight of  no more than 30 kg.
- Two workers, each with free access, can lift a total of about 45 kg.
If  access is difficult or weights exceed the above values, then provision must be made for lifting with a hoist, a forklift with slings or, in special cases, a mobile or overhead crane. All lifting equipment is included in the scope of  delivery.
In cases where electrical equipment is used, the Contractor may need to provide  trolleys or special chassis, which will need to be included in the scope of work if  it is not possible to provide other means.
If  it is not clear from the general arrangement diagram which way a piece of equipment should be delivered to the aisle, then this must be indicated separately. If any component is located at a high elevation, then the path of delivery of such component to the hard surface of the passage or to the road must be clearly indicated, if this is not clear from the existing layout.
If  it is planned to use an overhead crane for maintenance, this must be specifically provided for in the plan for the use of  cranes, indicating the location of  the cranes and equipment, indicating the load capacity of the equipment. The use of tooling with obviously higher load capacity for light parts should be avoided due to the difficulty of  access.
The clearance to the front work surface at the point of service must be at least 600 mm and preferably greater than 750 mm. In the case of pumps (or other rotating equipment), these clearances must be provided on both sides of  the pump center line. The technical documentation should provide for the possibility of  unhindered movement from the point of  performance of work to the passage.

The technological protection system of  the power plant must comply with the requirements of the legislation in the field of  industrial safety of  the Republic of  Kazakhstan.
The technological protection system of  the power plant must be fully automatic and prevent the occurrence and development of emergency situations by automatically generating and issuing control actions  on  actuators  and  switching  devices  for  emergency  transfer  of the  protected  technological equipment to a safe state in case of  violations of  the normal operating mode.
The technological protection system must have the highest priority in relation to all other control actions.
The technological protection system must be fault-tolerant. Failures ofindividual elements of  the protection system should not lead to emergency shutdowns when the backup channels are operational.
The  system  must  be  protected  from  electromagnetic  interference  (high  voltage  equipment, lightning, etc.).

chunks.text:
Fuel gas preparation equipment must ensure the normal operation of power plants,  both as a single unit and as a complete set.
The fuel system must ensure the supply of  fuel to the combustion chamber, its dosage according to the signals of  the control system, as well as the termination of  the fuel supply at the command of the operator or automatically  when the protections are triggered.  The system  must consist of dispensers, shut-off valves, fuel filters, necessary fittings, sensors and pipelines.
Depending on the type of equipment and the gas supply scheme, it may be necessary to build a gas compressor station, consisting of  at least 2 gas compressors. In this case, the gas compressor station and all necessary communications to and from it will be included in the Contractor's scope of supplies and work.
Compressors must be located in special ventilated rooms with noise suppressors that comply with noise standards. When performing a gas compressor station, it is necessary to provide all the necessary safety measures. Gas supply control equipment must be installed on the compressors to instantly provide the required level of  gas supply to the power plant equipment under conditions of the entire load range.
The compressor system must ensure that no pressure or flow changes are transmitted to the power plant equipment under any transient or steady states.
Compressors  and  their  ancillary  equipment  must  be  able  to  operate  in  the  full  range  of temperature  regimes  of gas  supply,  as  well  as  in  the  range  of pressures  and  temperatures  of  the environment in the area of  the power plant. For gas supply, it is necessary to provide for the installation of  a complete set of  instrumentation to ensure complete control of  the gas supply from the control panel of  the power plant, as well as to ensure appropriate control during start-ups, shutdowns and under normal operating conditions. Safe shutdown systems must provide protection for compressors and auxiliaries. Particular attention should be paid to transients caused by shutdowns of gas-using equipment.
Gas  compressors  must be  equipped  with  the necessary  lifting  equipment  for  installation  and scheduled  maintenance,  and  have  sufficient  space  to  accommodate  the  equipment  being  serviced. Compressors must respond to load shedding without shutting down. The performance of  each of  the gas compressors must provide 100% of  the required gas flow for the operation of the power plant equipment at rated load. It should be ensured that the backup gas compressor is automatically switched on when the operating compressor is stopped at any load without disconnecting the power plant equipment from the network.

To ensure safe and  reliable operation,  the unit must be equipped with a standard AVCVDS system  (automated  vibration  control  and  vibration  diagnostics  system).  The  system  should  include control and protection equipment and a computer monitoring system.
The computer monitoring system must ensure the collection and storage of  the data archive for at  least  one  year.  Transfer  current  and  archived  information  on  controlled  parameters  to  remote workstations via the local information network of  the enterprise for diagnostic purposes.  The system must ensure the collection and processing of  measurement results obtained from all channels in transient modes during the start and stop of  the machine (run-out). Have the possibility of  automated diagnostics of  the technical condition of  the unit and warning of  personnel about unfavorable trends in the change in the vibration state.
The units must be equipped with the following measuring elements:
Sensors  for measuring the absolute  vibration  of bearings  (at least two  per  support)  or stator elements of  the machine, the number and location of  their installation must comply with [OCT MCO 10816-4-2002 (GOST ISO 10816-4-2002).
Sensors for measuring relative shaft vibration, each radial bearing must be equipped with two sensors and located in accordance with fOCT HCO 7919-1-2002 (GOST ISO 7919-1-2002).
Each thrust bearing  must be equipped  with sensors to measure the absolute vibration of  the bearing in accordance with fOCT HCO 10817-1-2002 (GOST ISO 10817-1-2002).
To measure the relative vibration of  the shaft, each radial bearing must be equipped with two sensors according to [OCT 27165-97 (GOST 27165-97).
Each thrust bearing must be equipped with three rotor axial position sensors.
The machines must be equipped (if  necessary) with speed sensors, expansion sensors (absolute expansion of  the turbine housing and relative expansion of  the rotor), bearing support slope sensors that provide objective information about the thermal expansion of  the unit.
In addition, the unit must (if  necessary) be equipped with sensors for measuring the curvature of the unit's rotor shaft.
Engineering units for controlling shaft relative vibration must comply with fOCT HCO 7919-12002 (GOST ISO 7919-1-2002).

chunks.text:
The lubrication and control system of  the unit must ensure long-term reliable operation of  all its parts in all operating modes. The bid must contain a detailed description of  the oil system, including the oil cooling system and the method of  controlling its temperature.
To safely shut down the unit in the event of  a power failure, at least one emergency lube oil pump must be powered by DC power.
Standby and emergency oil pumps must be equipped with an automatic start system.
To filter the oil, full-flow filters (2 x 100%) are integrated into the lubrication system. Differential pressure gauges are installed on the line filters, alarm signals from which are given in the control room. Provides the ability to change the filter during operation. A spare set oflubricating oil filters is supplied for the commissioning period.
An oil  cleaning unit  must  be  provided.  It can  be a  motor-driven centrifuge  or  a  multi-stage purification system based on sedimentation and filtration. In any case, this unit must be placed on an oil collecting  pan  and  contain  filters,  controls,  control  panels,  ventilation  equipment  and  other  devices necessary for the normal operation of  this unit.
The Contractor shall provide for the installation of an emergency oil drain tank of sufficient capacity to receive all the oil when the system is emptied.
The removal oflubricating oil vapors from the oil tank must be carried out using fans and cleaned using  oil separator  filters.  The oil tank must be equipped with  graduated  level gauges (remotely and locally), oil drain fittings by gravity and an alarm device in case of  excessive level decrease and increase. It must be possible to increase the oil temperature after a long period of  inactivity.
Air-filled oil return lines must be made of  stainless steel.
The oil control  system  must be  fitted  with suitable  accumulators  or  equivalent  equipment  to withstand a transient and power interruption of  at least 5.0 seconds.
To filter non-flammable liquids, full-flow filters (2x100%) are built into the oil control system. Differential pressure gauges are installed on the filters, alarm signals from which are given in the control room. Provides the ability to change the filter during operation. A spare set of  filters for the control loop is supplied for the commissioning period.

chunks.text:
All  buildings  and  structures  must  have  complete  automated  heating,  ventilation  and  air conditioning (HV  AC) systems, consisting of  the necessary air conditioning units, fans, heaters, control units and other things.
All systems must be designed and installed to provide acceptable environmental conditions for each area. The conditions of temperature, humidity, air movement and air filtration must be controlled in accordance with the requirements in the respective premises.
The HV  AC systems should be designed to shut down in the event of a fire alarm, pressurize supply and exhaust ducts as required for clean agent fire extinguishing systems, and start pressurization systems.  Ventilation  and smoke  removal in the event of a fire must be provided in all areas of the installation using roof  vents or exhaust fans.
The  Contractor  shall  prepare  calculations  for  sizing  and  selecting  HV  AC  equipment  and components.  These  calculations  should  be  based  on,  but  not  limited  to,  environmental  design requirements. Heating and cooling load calculations must be made in accordance with the requirements of  the TNLA of  the Republic of  Kazakhstan.
The Contractor shall submit to the Customer the final engineering calculations of the system design,  approved  design  drawings  (air  flow  diagrams,  equipment  drawings  indicating  connecting dimensions) and equipment certificates.
The cooling load should include heat input from internal electrical and mechanical sources, solar heat input to buildings, and ventilation loads. The design must include at least a 10% capacity margin for heating and cooling loads.
The HV  AC equipment must be of industrial quality and designed for round-the-clock operation. All systems and components must be suitable for operation in harsh environments with high temperature and  humidity,  match  the  design  life  of the  power  plant,  be  designed  for  maximum  life  cycle  and complexity in accordance with the functional performance of the power plant, be easy to maintain and reliable.
Belts, pulleys, chains, gears, couplings, and protruding objects such as set screws, keys, and other rotating parts must be completely enclosed and positioned so that  personnel in the immediate vicinity are adequately protected.

The  Defect  list  is  an  integral  part  of the  completion  process  and  is  also  a  critical  step  in determining  the  completion status  of the  Facilities/Works.  The  category of items  of the  Defect  list determines the fact that the Facilities / Works are ready to move to the next stage. Items of the Defect list take precedence in the categories as specified in this section.
Twenty-one (21) days prior to the expected date of Mechanical readiness, the Contractor will provide  the  Customer  with  notice  of  the  readiness  of  the  facilities  for  a  joint  interim  inspection (hereinafter referred to as the Interim inspection) and of  the planned date of  the Mechanical readiness of the facilities. Unless otherwise agreed by the parties, an Interim inspection will take place more than ten (10) days prior to the expected Mechanical readiness date of  the facilities. The Contractor undertakes to be present during the Interim inspection at any reasonable time during these 10 (ten) days for the purpose of conducting and completing the Interim inspection.
Twenty-one (21  ) days before the expected date of  Completion of  pre-commissioning works, the Contractor will provide the Customer with a notice of the readiness of the facilities for the joint Final inspection (hereinafter referred to as the Final inspection) and of the planned date of Completion of the pre-commissioning works of the facilities. Unless otherwise agreed by the parties, the Final inspection will  not  take  place  more  than  ten  (10)  days  prior  to  the  expected  date  of  Completion  of  pre­ commissioning. The Contractor undertakes to be present during the Final inspection at any reasonable time within these 10 (ten) days for the purpose of conducting and completing the Final inspection.
The Contractor undertakes to take into account any comments, information and notices provided by the Customer in accordance with this section, as well as to make adjustments or otherwise eliminate any inconsistencies or errors to the extent required by the Customer.
Unless otherwise agreed, an Interim inspection and a Final inspection will be carried out and completed within 10 (ten) days following receipt of  the Contractor's notice in accordance with the time periods specified above, on the date or days specified by the Customer.
At the time of the Interim inspection on the day or days specified above, the parties shall draw up items of  the Defect list, which the Contractor undertakes to correct or amend. The Customer shall act in accordance with the terms of  this section and the Contract in determining the category of items of  the Defect list (Item of  the Defect list of  A category, Item of  the Defect list of  B category, Item of  the Defect list of C category and Item of the Defect list of D category), and may change the category of items of the Defect list from time to time.
When conducting a Final inspection, the parties must update the Defect list to reflect completed items of  the Defect list and identified items of  the Defect list.

When planning and conducting tests for compliance with guaranteed indicators, the Contractor shall comply with the requirements described in the form «Guaranteed indicators».
The  Contractor  allocates  for  planning  and  conducting  tests  for  compliance  with  guaranteed indicators, as well as for the preparation of reports on them by an independent, well-reviewed, qualified company (the «Testing company»). The choice and appointment of the Testing company is approved by the Customer.
During the tests, the power plant is operated by the Customer's personnel under the supervision of  the Contractor.
The  Contractor  describes  the  methodology  for  measuring  the  required  parameters,  and  also provides information on the expected standards and accuracy of  instrumentation, expected measurement points and attaches the necessary documentation.
For each case of  failure to achieve the guaranteed performance due to the fault of  the Contractor (manufacturer of goods), the Contractor shall pay a penalty in the amount specified in the Contract.
The output electrical power is measured in the high voltage cell of the switchgear.
Current and voltage transformers are supplied by the Contractor to measure useful output power, generator power and auxiliary power. They must generally comply with the requirements for equipment, except that the current transformers must have an accuracy class of 0.1, and voltage transformers must have  an  accuracy class of 0.2  according to  IEC  60044-1  and  IEC  60044-2.  The Contractor submits calibration documents for all transformers.
Power kilowatt-hour meters for own needs for efficiency and performance testing are provided by the  Contractor. These  meters  shall  comply  with  accuracy class  0.5  according to  IEC  60521  and accuracy class 0.5 according to IEC 60687. The current and voltage transformers associated with these kilowatt-hour meters are also supplied by the Contractor and comply with the standards specified in the Contract.
On HRSGs, tests are carried out for the purity of steam (water) on them. Tests are carried out at all loads using permanently installed high-speed samplers. Particular attention is paid to situations with a change in load or unstable conditions, when mechanical transfer is most likely.
A sample of the fuel used in the tests is taken at the beginning, during and at the end of  the tests for compliance with the guaranteed performance. The necessary equipment for taking and storing fuel samples is  supplied by the  Contractor. During each sampling period,  three separate  samples will be taken,  i.e. a  total of nine  samples will be taken.  One  sample  from  each set  of three  samples is  fully analyzed by an independent body, the costs of  such analyzes are borne by the Contractor. The other two samples from each set are duly labeled and handed over to the Customer.

The Contractor will prepare and implement a detailed Air quality management plan as part of  the ESMP. The plan  will detail all environmental mitigation measures that the Contractor will implement during the  construction period to reduce harmful impacts caused by air emissions and dust generation from construction activities, including from traffic on access roads. The plan will also include specific measures to reduce greenhouse gas emissions.
The Contractor will take at least the following measures to control dust and other emissions from construction activities:
- Good maintenance of access roads that will be used for a long time.
- Strict  control of dirt roads  and  other  dust-producing areas by  spraying with  water  under  dry weather conditions for dust suppression.
- Keep the drop height of  potentially dusty materials as low as possible.
- Ensure that a wheel washer is available and used to avoid spreading dust to neighboring roads via construction trucks.
- Apply speed limits in the area.
- Do not allow the engine of construction machines to run in the parking lot and without use.
- Use well maintained equipment and machines in accordance with the methods specified by the manufacturer.
- Ensure regular technical inspection of  used construction machines, mechanisms and vehicles for minimum exhaust emissions.
- The use of electricity for the technical needs of construction (heating of materials, heating of water) instead of solid and liquid fuels.
- Use of special vehicles and containers for storage, loading and transportation of bulk, dusty and wet materials.

The Contractor will prepare and implement a detailed Noise and vibration management plan as part of the ESMP.  The  plan will describe how  the  Contractor will minimize and manage noise and vibration impacts during construction.
The Contractor will take at least the following measures to mitigate the negative impact of  noise and vibration at construction sites:
- Regular inspection and maintenance of all machines and vehicles.
- Installation of  mufflers or acoustic guards on machines where applicable, such as fitting suitable mufflers to engine exhaust pipes and compressor components, and use of portable sound barriers (if  required).
- Implement speed limits for trucks traveling to and from construction sites.
- Route shortening project traffic through public areas where possible.
- Installation of shock absorbers to dampen vibrations.
- Placement of working machines and mechanisms on the construction site, taking into account mutual protection from noise and natural barriers.
- Installation of silencers on air intakes, vibration isolators and vibration dampers on compressor units.

The purpose of  communications management is to establish, streamline and implement clear and effective means of communication that will facilitate the processing of information between all parties associated  with  the  Project.  Effective  communications  management  ensures  the  completeness  of documentation for legal,  fiscal,  administrative and historical purposes  (project review, audits, claims, etc.).
Effective communication is a key element to the success of a project, as it ensures that all team members are informed of  the decisions made in a timely manner. Communications management ensures that all relevant stakeholders receive the information they need effectively and in a timely manner.
Communication on the project can be carried out in the form of  printed and electron_ic documents, informal and formal meetings:
Provide timely guidance to the parties involved in the project:
- Ensure that project stakeholders are informed and given the opportunity to contribute in a timely manner and agree to project decisions;
- Ensure timely provision of  accurate project information to all project stakeholders;
- Monitor and coordinate other communications for internal or external audiences.
The day-to-day exchange of information will take place, as a rule, between the Contractor and the Customer.

chunks.text:
The communications management process will be governed by the Communications management plan, which will be prepared by the Contractor and approved by the Customer. This plan will  outline  how  communications  will  be  maintained  throughout  the  life  of  the  project.  The communication requirements will be documented in a responsibility matrix to be developed prior to the start of  the project.
Language: The language used in all written communications under the Contract relating to all items of service offered by all parties must be written in both Russian and English.
Units of Measure: The units of  measure for the project and all related documentation must be in metric units.
Form  of  communications: Communications  include  submission  of  engineering, design, procurement and construction documentation, calculations, reports, letters,  accompanying documents, memorandums and minutes of  meetings.
Reference Acquaintance: All written correspondence must have a specific reference code, and replies must reference this code. The Gregorian calendar is used in the format day, month, year (either 06.08.2022 or August 06, 2022).
Oral communication: All formal oral communications must be confirmed in writing as soon as possible.
Acknowledgment of receipt: Receipt of all documents and correspondence must be confirmed by signature and seal.
All documents and correspondence should be on standard communication forms to ensure the flow of information is managed. For all forms of communication, logs should be kept indicating the originator, recipient, date of  issue, date of  response required, days when no response was received, and these logs should be issued and transmitted by the originator.
The aim is to monitor the responsiveness of the parties and avoid or minimize late responses that affect the project.

This section briefly outlines the main project management tools. The project management tools discussed in this section provide the basis for quantifying the scope, schedule, and budget for all phases of a project. These tools will provide timely and accurate information describing the status of Project activities and will be helpful in formulating corrective actions for potential problems.
In this regard, the Contractor shall hire qualified and experienced personnel competent in the preparation of  an integrated project program, cost, allocation of  resources (manpower, plant/equipment, materials, etc.) and development of a baseline plan for monitoring and measuring performance.

chunks.text:
Hierarchical structure of  works (hereinafter referred to as the HSW) provides a logical framework for project management planning, reporting and control, and has been prepared to describe the Program with an increasing level of detail for adequate management visibility. The HSW covers all phases of  the project and provides a consistent coding structure throughout, accommodating the various requirements of all parts of  the Program.
The HSW reflects the set of works to be performed by the Contractor and all third parties that may be involved in the Program. The HSW will be a common identifier between time/cost/documents and will be used to ensure integration of  time, cost, document and program resource elements.
The Contractor will install a HSW that will allow structuring information about the project at different levels of detail for different organizations. The HSW will include an alphanumeric numbering system that uniquely identifies each element of the HSW, ensuring transparency in both directions (top to bottom and bottom to top). The Contractor shall submit the Hierarchical structure of works (HSW) to the Customer for approval.
The  Contractor  will be responsible for  including  the  appropriate  WDS  number in the master schedule, organizing and grouping works according to the approved structure. The Contracting Surveyor will  include  the  same structure  in  the  Cost  Coding  System to  accurately  reflect  all  associated  costs budgeted, accepted and expended. In this way, he can develop cost reports related to budget/cost incurred at each level of the HSW structure, which will now be converted to a cost breakdown structure (CBS). The Contractor warrants that:
- The HSW includes all the tasks that must be completed during the implementation phases of  the project. The HSW is developed using the software application and hosted on a server.
- The HSW identifier (alphanumeric) is included in the cost breakdown structure to provide integration between time, cost, and documents.
- The  HSW  identifier  (alphanumeric)  is  entered  into  all  documents  to  identify  all documents and allow integration with the above parameters (cost, schedule, and documents).
The advantage of  having all three control components linked together via a WDS number allows close monitoring of project progress at all times, and easy access and monitoring of emerging issues.

chunks.text:
- Linking all three (3) components to the HSW identifier project will allow for a better and more  closed,  controlled  method  of measuring  day-to-day  progress  as  well  as  emerging  issues  and impacts that will occur during the course of  the work.
- All reports related to Schedule/Cost/Documents must include the HSW identifier.
- Reports should also be generated and grouped using the HSW code for easy access to project/task information reporting issues based on time, cost, or related documents related to any specific HSW code number.

Project budget management consists of  developing and maintaining a budget, as well as reporting and controlling costs at each stage of project development in accordance with the budget and cash flow, in order to avoid delays and cost overruns.
The main goal of  budgeting is to establish a balance between the developed and approved budget at  the  tender  stage  and  realized  costs  in  order  to  effectively  manage  the  design,  procurement  and execution processes to achieve the set goal.
The  Contractor  shall  structure  the  project  budget  with  a  cost  breakdown  structure  (CBS,  in accordance with the project HSW)  and submit to the Customer for approval. Such a structured budget
would effectively control the procurement process of  each work package, as well as control the project development (project manufacturability and cost-effectiveness, specifications and selection of  materials, etc.) associated with the work packages, in order to maintain budget limits and goals.
The budget and cash flows shall be updated and compared with previous and initial versions by the Contractor at each design stage and for each commitment, as well as during the procurement process. To track progress, you can plan actions to address any overflows; The following activities can be directed towards meeting budget objectives.
The set of  information and assumptions on which the budget is based should be documented so that  any  changes  in  these  criteria  and  assumptions  can  be  tracked  along  with  improvements  in  the information available. This will allow you to identify deviations in advance and allow you to calculate the cost for other budget items.

The Contractor shall prepare and  submit a resource-laden (manpower, equipment, materials, cost) level 3 project program showing the design, procurement, construction, testing and commissioning activities, milestones, critical paths and planned subcontracting activities to the Customer within 28 days after receipt of  the Work start notice. The term for consideration of  documents will not exceed 21 days from the date of  receipt of  the project program of  the construction Contractor with the form of  transfer.
The  Customer shall  review  the Project program  and each revised program submitted by the Contractor and may send a Notice to the Contractor stating the extent to which it does not comply with the Contract, or ceases to reflect actual progress, or otherwise does not comply with the Contractor's plan of  commitment. If  the Customer fails to provide such Notice:
- within 21 days ofreceiving the initial program; or
- within 14 days of  receipt of  the revised program, the Customer shall be deemed to have given a No objection notice and the original program or the revised program (as applicable) shall be accepted as the approved Program.
Once the Project schedule has been approved and agreed upon, it replaces and governs the Application to the Contract, the Preliminary work schedule, as the Base schedule. The baseline schedule will contain  an  integrated  detailed  design,  procurement,  construction  and  testing  and  commissioning schedule for the Project and will be used to track the progress of  the project. The base schedules will be revised (rebased) only if  significant changes are made with the approval of  the Customer. A Basic level 3 schedule should include the following modules, as well as any individual tasks.
- Design  schedule:  The  design  module  should  be  prepared  taking  into  account  all engineering, survey, engineering and design work and all project deliverables, including key milestones for all contractual obligations.
- Procurement  schedule:  The  Procurement  Module  should  be  formulated  considering procurement, fabrication, delivery times, project timeframes for each procurement task, including key
milestones for all contractual obligations. Consideration and approval of the submitted materials/equipment/plan will be linked to the activities.
- Construction schedule:  The  Construction  module  shall  be developed in  detail  for  all construction  works,  taking  into  account  the  logical  sequence  and  duration  of the  Works,  including requirements for procurement time, quantities, resources, adhering to the established HSW structure by the Contractor at a lower level of detail with key milestones included for all contractual obligations.

The Document management system  (DMS) will be implemented  using automated  electronic document management tools in combination with paper archives of documents in accordance with the overall management structure of  the HSW system. Records Management will allow Program participants to exercise greater control over the production, storage and distribution of documents, improving the ability  to  reuse information,  control the  flow of documents  and  reduce lead times.  The  full range of
functions that a document management system (DMS) must perform includes document identification, storage and retrieval, tracking, versioning, workflow management, and presentation.
The elements of  the DMS that must be implemented for a project include the software, hardware, and procedures to perform all the functions necessary to manage records in projects from initiation, or whenever they are introduced in a project, to completion. Each element is described below.

Addressee: This part of  the form indicates the name and address of the organization to indicate the addressee.
Subject:  Each  letter  should  have  only one  subject,  and for  submission  purposes,  the  subject should be written correctly and clearly. The subject should summarize the content of the letter, and no other irrelevant definitions should be written in this part.
Attachment: Appropriate attachments submitted with the Letter should be listed in this section below the Letter.
To: The letter should be addressed to the project director or responsible person. This part should remain unchanged until the end of  the project term, unless new responsible persons are appointed for the specified responsibility.
Copy: If the letter is planned to be duplicated to another person/party, this part is filled in with the name of the specified person/party.
Cover letter: All types of documents, files, reports, charts, etc., which must be sent along with the letter, are considered an «attachment». A document designated as an attachment must be attached to both the letter and the copy. The Original attachment is attached to the letter, which remains with the recipient.
Delivery:  Letters to be delivered by hand  must be prepared as two copies:  the original must remain with the recipient and the copy must be signed as «received» along with the date, time and name of  the recipient.

The Contractor shall develop and implement a risk management approach in accordance with the international standard ISO 31000:2018 «Risk Management - Principles and Guidelines», as well as other ISO standards that supplement it, including, but not limited to: ISO/ TR 31004:2013 «Guidelines for implementation of  the ISO 31000 standard», ISO 31010:2019 «Risk assessment methods».
The Contractor's risk management process shall include three interrelated approaches as shown below:
- Systematic and continuous identification of factors (sources, drivers, triggers) of risks, identification of exposure to risk,  assessment of the nature, likelihood and potential impact of  risks on the Project.
- Planning and organizing the necessary measures for the treatment of  risks of  the Project: reducing the likelihood of risks, transferring risks, as well as methods of  financing risks to minimize damage from risk realization;
- Implementation of  risk management methods within the organization at all levels of  the Project implementation, as well as outside it: working with insurance organizations, loss containment specialists and other risk financing specialists.
The following table (Table 1. Risk Management Plan) shows examples of the main risk areas and risk management approaches that the Contractor should identify, assess and manage.
Project cost, Management approach = Cost control program for project management, cost optimization, work schedule; Change Management Process. Work schedule, Management approach = Analysis of a constructive solution by an engineer; opportunities, previously started tasks, management of key resources, management of deadlines compared to the estimated duration of work. Project quality, Management approach = Contractor's quality assurance programs; supply quality management, non-compliance act management / corrective and preventive actions. System integration, Management approach = Integration and optimization of electrical and mechanical systems, consideration ofthe design solution and design criteria. Worker injury/environmental accident, Management approach = Contractor's zero accident preventive health and safety program, pre-job hazard analysis, health and safety instructions, training

The Customer shall develop a procedure that defines the methodology and the associated roles and responsibilities for the control of  nonconformities related to the product and the quality process. The procedure should include a format for documenting nonconformities (Nonconformity Report Form). The Contractor will be required to implement this procedure.
If defects in material,  work  performed or  installation  are found, the Customer will notify the Contractor by issuing a Non-Conformity Report (NCR). Upon receipt of such notice, the Contractor shall immediately take steps to prevent the inadvertent use or supply of  certain nonconforming material, work or installation.
Upon receipt of the NCR, the Contractor shall immediately investigate the matter and prepare corrective actions in relation to measures to eliminate the identified non-conformities and submit them to the Customer for review and approval.
If the Customer approves the proposed corrective actions, the Contractor shall implement the proposed measures and upon completion resubmit the NCR to the Customer for closure.
The Contractor and suppliers effectively apply documented procedures that ensure that any non­ conforming product is prevented from unintended use or installation.
The  Contractor  shall  maintain  a  Register  of Nonconformities  to  indicate  the  status  of  all nonconformities that have been identified by the Customer and the Contractor. The Customer reserves the right to inspect and audit these documents at any time.

Each  report  shall  include,  as  appropriate,  proposed  measures  to improve and/or correct the QC System and/or its implementation.
In addition,  the Customer has the right to audit any aspect of the quality management system (QMS) of the Contractor's project, in accordance with the requirements oflSO 19011  :2011. These will include audits of quality system elements, audits of products and services, and audits of processes and technical procedures.
The Customer can conduct scheduled and unscheduled inspections and quality audits. When conducting scheduled audits, the Contractor will be notified of the quality audit at least five (05) days in advance.
